catalog_quote: Seri, a language isolate spoken in northwestern Mexico, regularly assigns stress to the penultimate syllable of a root; affixes are not relevant for determining the placement of stress. A heavy final syllable in the root attracts stress, however, although a final consonant is extrametrical. ... Some roots have extrametrical final syllables and a few roots have exceptional stress. ... The stress pattern is affected by the weight of a syllable. When the last syllable in the domain has a long vowel, a diphthong, or a complex coda, that syllable is stressed. ... the final consonant does not contribute to the syllable weight for this purpose ... final consonant is extrametrical (Hayes 1982, Hayes 1995). As a result, a final syllable with a simple coda is light for the purposes of foot construction. ... stress placement is based on the construction of a moraic trochee at the right edge of the…
sweep_summary: Seri (seri1257) sweep: two title hits, both by Marlett and both the same analysis. (1) Marlett 2008 (Linguistic Discovery 6.1, the catalog's deciding source) was already held; re-read and copied to the audit folder; it confirms the 'weight' coding verbatim (root-domain moraic trochee, penultimate default, heavy final attracts stress, final C extrametrical, lexical extrametrical syllables, exceptions). (2) Marlett 2006 'El acento, la extrametricalidad y la palabra mínima en seri' (Santa Rosa conference proceedings, Spanish) was NOT held; fetched sources live from lengamer.org (HTTP 200, 9-pp text-layer PDF,, logged). It is the Spanish original that 2008 expands: same rule, same examples, explicitly restricted to nouns and without the phonetics/audio section -> 'refines' (confirms coding; earlier, narrower scope). Nothing to acquire; no priority items. The catalog's deciding source (2008) stands; 2006 should be added to the per-language bibliography as its antecedent.

new_statements.quote: Los siguientes ejemplos muestran que el acento normalmente cae en la penúltima sílaba de palabras multisilábicas. ... Cuando la última sílaba tiene una vocal larga o una coda compleja, esta sílaba (generalmente) atrae el acento. Por lo tanto, sabemos que seri es una lengua sensible a la cantidad ... Entonces propongo que la última consonante es extrametrical ... he propuesto que el acento en los sustantivos se basa en un pie trocaico construido al lado derecho de la raíz. La última consonante de la raíz no cuenta para este propósito. La última sílaba es pesada solamente si tiene dos vocales (o más) en el núcleo o dos consonantes (o más) en la coda.
new_statements.translation: The following examples show that stress normally falls on the penultimate syllable of polysyllabic words. ... When the last syllable has a long vowel or a complex coda, that syllable (generally) attracts stress. So we know Seri is a quantity-sensitive language ... I therefore propose that the final consonant is extrametrical ... I have proposed that stress in nouns is based on a trochaic foot built at the right edge of the root. The final consonant of the root does not count for this purpose. The final syllable is heavy only if it has two (or more) vowels in the nucleus or two (or more) consonants in the coda.

new_statements.reading: Weight-sensitive right-edge system within the root: penultimate by default, final if the root-final syllable is heavy (VV nucleus or CC coda; a single final consonant is extrametrical), plus lexical extrametrical syllables and a residue of exceptions. Identical to the catalog's 'weight' coding. It is the earlier, Spanish, nouns-only version of the deciding source.

sources.note: This is the catalog's deciding source, re-read in full. Domain = root (affixes irrelevant, sect. 8); a moraic trochee at the right edge of the root gives penultimate stress by default; a root-final syllable that is heavy (long vowel/diphthong, or complex coda; a single final consonant is extrametrical) takes stress; some roots have lexically extrametrical final syllables (antepenultimate stress, sect. 7); a residue of exceptions (final light-syllable stress, penultimate stress despite a final CC coda, and many verbs) is listed in sect. 9. sources.note: Spanish conference-paper original of the 2008 article (2008 fn.1 calls itself 'an expansion of Marlett (2006a)'). Same analysis: root is the domain (prefixes never stressed except by vowel fusion), right-edge trochaic foot -> penultimate default, heavy final syllable (long vowel/diphthong or CC coda) attracts stress, single final C extrametrical, a short list of lexically extrametrical final syllables (antepenultimate, ex. 15), and residual exceptions (hamác, coláxö, coqué... ex. 18). sources.quote: 'The accent usually falls on the first syllable of the root. We consider this as the default position and other positions as lexical exceptions. In compounds and in phrases, the primary stress is generally the final one, although other factors are also involved.' This is the author's pre-2008 root-initial analysis (= Marlett 1981 rule (3), Marlett 1987/1988), which Marlett 2008 sect. 2 'Previous analyses' explicitly replaces with the right-edge moraic-trochee/weight analysis our record codes; agrees on the root domain and on affixes being irrelevant, differs on edge and weight.
